2.description: Collections, exception handling, multi-threading, and Java streams.

questions.question_text: What will be the output of this code snippet utilizing wrapper caching?
Which interface must a class implement to allow its objects to be sorted using `Collections.sort()` without a custom Comparator?
What happens when an exception is thrown inside a `try` block that has both a `catch` block and a `finally` block?
options: The finally block runs before the catch block
The catch block runs first, then the finally block runs
The finally block is skipped if catch handles the exception

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between an `ArrayList` and a `LinkedList` in Java?
options: ArrayList uses a doubly-linked list; LinkedList uses a dynamic array
ArrayList provides O(1) random access; LinkedList provides O(1) insertions/deletions when node reference is known
LinkedList is synchronized by default; ArrayList is not

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the `volatile` keyword in Java multi-threading?
options: It locks methods to prevent race conditions like synchronized
It guarantees that changes to a variable are immediately visible to other threads (prevents CPU caching)
It deletes objects from memory automatically

questions.question_text: Which collection type does NOT allow duplicate elements and guarantees unique entries based on `equals()` and `hashCode()`?
What will this stream operation output?
Can an interface in Java have method bodies?
options: No, all methods in an interface must be strictly abstract
Yes, using the `default` or `static` keywords introduced in Java 8
Only if the interface is marked as abstract

questions.question_text: What is the primary behavior of a `HashMap` when a key collision occurs (two keys hash to the same bucket)?
options: The old value is instantly deleted
An exception is thrown crashing the map
Entries are stored in a linked list or balanced tree (Java 8+) at that bucket index
The map automatically increases its bucket capacity to infinity

questions.question_text: What is a functional interface in Java?
options: An interface containing exactly one abstract method
An interface used exclusively for math operations
An interface that cannot be implemented

3.description: Advanced memory management, concurrency, class initialization, and bytecode.

questions.question_text: What will be the output or behavior of executing this code involving class initialization order?
How does Java’s Garbage Collector handle objects referenced only by a `WeakReference`?
options: They are never collected until the application shuts down
They are collected during the next garbage collection cycle regardless of available heap memory
They are collected only when the JVM runs critically low on memory
They are promoted to the old generation pool

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of the `happens-before` relationship in the Java Memory Model (JMM)?
options: It enforces that code execution order matches written line numbers strictly
It guarantees that memory writes by one statement are visible to another statement, preventing instruction reordering issues in concurrent execution
It dictates which thread starts first

questions.question_text: What is the structural difference between a `ThreadLocal` variable and a standard shared variable in multi-threaded environments?
options: ThreadLocal provides a separate, isolated copy of the variable for each individual thread accessing it
ThreadLocal automatically synchronizes writes across all CPU cores
ThreadLocal stores variables directly in CPU registers
There is no difference; it is an alias for synchronized

questions.question_text: What is bytecode weaving in the context of Java frameworks like AspectJ or Spring AOP?
options: Compiling Java source code into machine code via JIT
Modifying existing class bytecode bytes (either at compile-time, load-time, or runtime) to inject cross-cutting behavior like logging or transactions
Encrypting jar files to prevent decompilation
A memory optimization technique for garbage collection

questions.question_text: What happens when you call `intern()` on a dynamically created `String` object in Java?
options: It creates a deep copy of the string on the heap
It checks if the string exists in the JVM String Pool; if so, it returns a reference to that pooled instance, otherwise it adds it to the pool
It converts the string to lowercase UTF-8 format
It forces the string to be garbage collected

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of using Java NIO (Non-blocking I/O) Channels and Buffers over traditional IO Streams?
options: NIO automatically encrypts all network packets
NIO allows multiplexed, non-blocking asynchronous operations where a single thread can manage multiple active network connections
NIO bypasses the operating system kernel entirely

questions.question_text: In the Java Concurrency package, what does a `CountDownLatch` do?
options: It acts as a mutual exclusion lock like a semaphore with a count of 1
It allows one or more threads to wait until a set of operations being performed in other threads completes
It counts how many threads have deadlocked
It automatically terminates background worker threads

questions.question_text: What is the core difference between `ClassNotFoundException` and `NoClassDefFoundError` in Java?
options: ClassNotFoundException is a checked exception thrown when an application tries to load a class by name at runtime but it cannot be found; NoClassDefFoundError is an unchecked error thrown when a class was present at compile-time but missing at runtime
ClassNotFoundException only occurs in multithreaded environments
NoClassDefFoundError can be caught using a standard catch block safely

questions.question_text: What is a `Spliterator` introduced in Java 8 primarily designed to achieve?
options: Splitting text strings into regex arrays
Traversing and partitioning elements of a source (especially for parallel stream processing and data splitting)
Splitting database transactions into smaller threads
Replacing standard iterators in legacy codebases
